vm_tools: maitred: Add support to wait for processes When setting up the environment for running containers we need to perform some steps serially and we need to ensure that each step completed successfully before continuing on to the next one. To address this, add a new option to the LaunchProcess RPC to wait until the launched process exits. If this option is set the RPC will also return information about how the process exited (exited normally or killed by signal). BUG=none TEST=Spawn some processes with the wait_for_exit flag set and see that everything works. Change-Id: Ia0edd5c3c4ec96a55812f9a4cb438ee618399465 Signed-off-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/658143 Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

vm_tools: maitred: Fix signal handling in child processes Maitred blocks all signals before forking to prevent the child from accidentally handling signals meant for the parent. While these signals are eventually unblocked in the parent process, they are not unblocked in the child process leading to all spawned processes ignoring every signal except SIGKILL and SIGSTOP, which cannot be blocked. Fix this by resetting all signal handlers to their default dispositions in the child process before exec-ing. BUG=none TEST=manual. Spawn a new process, send it SIGTERM, and see that it actually terminates. Change-Id: Ie389add8cd212af98c53d06b85a8c04f62e86321 Signed-off-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/668093 Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

vm_tools: maitred: Improve child process error handling Right now if a failure occurs in one of the steps that run in the child process after it forks but before it executes the requested program we don't have any way of finding out about it. The only thing the parent process sees is that the child exited with a non-zero status. Improve the error handling by using a socketpair to communicate any setup failures back to the parent process. After forking, the parent process blocks on a read on one end of the socketpair while the child process does its setup. If any step fails, the child process writes a struct with the error details to its end of the socketpair. If all steps succeed the child process will not write anything to the socket and its end will be closed on a successful exec because the socketpair is created with the SOCK_CLOEXEC flag. This means that if the parent reads 0 bytes from the socket then the child process successfully executed the requested program. BUG=none TEST=manual Change-Id: I8a4b1c4a5f5c8054464649e1609382a504d65a7f Signed-off-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/668094 Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: btusb: remove HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER bit This removes the HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER bit from the Intel USB driver block in btusb_probe(). There is a conflict intention on receiving advertising reports in BlueZ where the Filter_Duplicates flag is set so strict filtering with RSSI will be applied to Intel BT controllers. However, BlueZ checks if HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER is set and restarts LE scan if the bit is set in order to obtain the advertising reports dropped due to the strict filtering. By removing the bit, BlueZ will not frequently restart LE scanning. BUG=b:64731753 TEST=emerge-eve sys-kernel/chromeos-kernel-4_4 ./update_kernel.sh --remote <IP to DUT> Make sure /sys/kernel/debug/bluetooth/hci0/quirk_strict_duplicate_filter on DUT is "N". CQ-DEPEND=CL:677741 Change-Id: Id14e4e1ea3a3d0d9eac448f341bb839ebf4d373f Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/677740 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>

CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: set Filter_Duplicates parameter to 0x00 for LE scanning This sets the Filter_Duplicates parameter of LE Set Scan Enable command to LE_SCAN_FILTER_DUP_DISABLE (0x00). There is a conflict intention of receiving advertising reports in BlueZ where the Filter_Duplicates flag is set so the strict filtering with RSSI will be applied to Intel BT controllers. However BlueZ checks if HCI_QUIRK_STRICT_DUPLICATE_FILTER is set and restarts LE scan if the bit is set in order to obtain the advertising reports dropped due to the strict filtering. By setting the Filter_Duplicates, BlueZ can potentially receive more advertising reports. BUG=b:64731753 TEST=emerge-eve sys-kernel/chromeos-kernel-4_4 ./update_kernel.sh --remote <IP to DUT> Confirms that the number of advertising reports increases in HCI traffics. CQ-DEPEND=CL:677740 Change-Id: Ic79c2c224d291b45f299295761bd7c19c8e19df5 Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/677741 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>

CHROMIUM: Add suspend-to-idle support in dark resume driver Currently dark resume driver only supports S3 and does not support suspend-to-idle. This is a serious limitation for S0ix enabled systems as they use suspend-to-idle mechanism. This limitation is there because the dark resume driver uses syscore ops that are only called for legacy ACPI S3 flows. On S0ix enabled systems dark_resume_enabled flag never gets set since .suspend method does not get called. This patch fixes the issue and uses pm_notifiers to support S3 and S0ix both. BUG=b:38400592 TEST=build and boot, activate_short_dark_resume and check that the device enters dark resume. gerrit: deps: handle edge cases better When looking up the gerrit dependencies, we might run into a CL that is based on a commit that did not go through Gerrit (e.g. a bot push). In that case, Gerrit won't know about the change, so searches for it will return no results, and our indexing subsequently fails. Ignore missing results for Gerrit deps, but display an error for user specified ones. Similarly, do not assume that the last result of the query is exactly the one we want. If the CQ-DEPEND is a Gerrit Change-Id, that could be the same across different repos/branches. We simply have to match them all since there's no way to disambiguate. BUG=chromium:767284 TEST=`gerrit deps 676525` no longer fails Change-Id: Id1212e402137fdbd076c83ef26a8e5a551d92bdd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/676177 Commit-Ready: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Paul Hobbs <phobbs@google.com>

power: use RTC-relative wakeup timeouts for suspend Most of our suspend/resume testing tools (powerd_suspend and suspend_stress_test) use the relative form to set wakealarms (write "+X" to '/sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm', where 'X' is the time offset). This allows the kernel to determine the RTC time to pass down to the device. However, powerd_dbus_suspend for some reason computes an absolute time, using the current system time. This mostly works fine if the system clock and the RTC are closely in sync, but it creates problems if the RTC is significantly leading/lagging. Let's be consistent, and just use the relative form. Noticed while bringing up an EC-based RTC on STM32 (CL:674054). BUG=b:63908519 TEST=`powerd_dbus_suspend --wakeup_timeout=10` Change-Id: I2d39f7160dcd85ef9c6c49fa80647289f41e4279 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/677625 Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>
